_README: This is a REFERENCE TEMPLATE, not a file LDO reads. A workflow has no filesystem access, so config reaches it only via args.config at invocation. Two ways to use this: (1) copy the values into your project's CLAUDE.md so Claude passes them on every run — /ldo-init writes that block for you; (2) pass them inline: Workflow({name:'ldo', args:{task:'...', config:{...}}}). Model names mean whatever your setup routes them to.
_models_note: planner and reviewer are 'opus' in every tier on purpose. Complexity is the Planner's own output, so it structurally can't gate its own model — only the 'medium' row's planner value is ever actually read at runtime (Research and Plan run before complexity is known). Reviewer is opus everywhere because a cheap reviewer that trusts the coder isn't a review, regardless of task size — coder is the one role that's actually meant to scale down.

_phases._comment: Plan, Code, and Review always run. Two are conditional.
_phases.security: runs when the Planner rates security_surface 'elevated'; force with security: true/false or securityByDefault

_securityByDefault: Not set here on purpose. Omit the key and the Planner decides (Security runs when it rates the surface 'elevated'). Add "securityByDefault": true to always threat-model, or false to never — either value overrides the Planner.
